Wrangler can create the resources your Worker needs during `wrangler deploy`, so you don't have to make them first. Cloudflare's current configuration docs list Queues among the supported types, alongside KV, R2, and D1. Older pages and the launch changelog mention only KV, R2, and D1, so the Queues support is newer.

**How it works**
- Add bindings to your config file without IDs. For R2, leave out the bucket name. To use this feature, add bindings to your configuration file without adding resource IDs, or in the case of R2, a bucket name.
- Running `wrangler dev` creates local versions of these resources, which persist between runs. When you run wrangler dev, local resources will automatically be created which persist between runs.
- Running `wrangler deploy` creates the remote resources and writes their IDs back to your config. When you run wrangler deploy, resources will be created for you, and their IDs will be written back to your configuration file.
- Resource names use the Worker name as a prefix. Resources will be created with the name of your worker as the prefix.

**Version and opt-out**
- The feature launched as an open beta for KV, R2, and D1. To use this feature, update to wrangler@4.45.0 and add bindings to your config file without resource IDs. The changelog also notes that you can disable the feature using the --no-x-provision flag.

**Deploying from the dashboard or Git**
- If you deploy from the dashboard, for example through GitHub, the resources are created, but their IDs are only visible in the dashboard. Currently, these resource IDs will not be written back to your repository.

**Example config**
A minimal config without IDs looks like this:
```jsonc
"kv_namespaces": [{ "binding": "CACHE" }],
"r2_buckets": [{ "binding": "ASSETS" }],
"d1_databases": [{ "binding": "DB" }]
```
This is adapted from a third-party skill page, not Cloudflare's docs, so verify the exact shape against the official configuration reference.

**Caveats**
- Some third-party pages list flags such as `--x-provision` and `--x-auto-create`. I could not confirm these in Cloudflare's own docs, so check your installed Wrangler version with `wrangler deploy --help` before relying on them.
- Because the feature is in beta, the supported resource list and flags may change. The current Cloudflare configuration page is the most reliable reference.

content.text:
Yes, with recent Wrangler versions (4.45.0 and later). This is called automatic resource provisioning. For KV, add the binding to your config without an `id`. When you run `wrangler deploy`, Wrangler creates the namespace, names it with your Worker's name as a prefix, and writes the new ID back into your config file. Cloudflare's current configuration docs also list Queues as supported, along with R2, D1 and a few others. Queues support is newer than the October 2025 launch, which covered only KV, R2 and D1, and the feature is still in beta. On an older Wrangler, or with `--no-x-provision`, it won't create anything, so you'd have to create them yourself first with `wrangler kv namespace create` and `wrangler queues create`. If you deploy from the dashboard or a Git integration, the resources still get created, but their IDs aren't written back to your repo.

Sources:
- [Automatic resource provisioning changelog (2025-10-24)](https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/2025-10-24-automatic-resource-provisioning/)
- [Wrangler configuration docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/configuration/)
